solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sonata, perhaps, large in sound — one of the later movements?

parts.note: Beethoven's Moonlight is a famous example of a sonata

indicators.note: the letter for large is placed in the middle of the word for healthy

parts.note: sound in the sense of healthy, in good shape
L is the standard clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A musician wonders which part of a piano sonata comes later in the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movements' suggests a sonata's sections, but the definition is a move made late at night. A MOONLIGHT FLIT is British slang for leaving home secretly at night, usually to dodge rent or debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping away from lodgings under cover of darkness is a removal made late at night, hence a later movement.

clue.text: Pass entrance exam in unusual show of actual merit

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of these two words appear in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An applicant gets through the entrance test by an odd display of real ability.
explanation.definitionFit: To matriculate is to enrol at a university, traditionally after passing its admission requirements.

clue.text: Love story about Democrat — it's a classic?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the round letter

indicators.note: the love-plus-falsehood pair goes about, around, the Democrat letter

parts.note: a story can be a falsehood, a lie

explanation.surface: A romantic tale involving a Democratic politician is asked about as a possible classic.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is a well-loved old song or film, something of a classic.

clue.text: Dog swallowing unknown quantities? One's an idle creature

indicators.note: the dog takes the two algebra letters into its middle

parts.note: a Lab is a Labrador retriever
in algebra the unknowns are usually written as z and y
read as 'ones', plural of one

explanation.surface: A dog that gulps things down is called an idle animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is an informal name for a lazy, idle person.

clue.text: Covering man carrying weapon

indicators.note: the word for man holds the weapon inside it

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A man is armed but somehow concealed beneath a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is an item of clothing, something that covers the body.

clue.text: Light rent reduced with support of church

indicators.note: in a down entry the church abbreviation sits beneath and supports what comes before
reduced means the word for torn loses its last letter

parts.note: rent as the past participle of rend, torn

explanation.surface: A tenant's rent is lowered with help from the local church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like housing costs, but here it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light, either a flaming brand or a battery flashlight.

clue.text: Schedule includes a lot from bombastic leader of service

indicators.note: the word for schedule holds the shortened word inside it

parts.note: a schedule is a list

indicators.note: a lot from means most of the word, all but its last letter

parts.note: bombastic speech is turgid, inflated

explanation.surface: A timetable contains most of a pompous speech by the person leading worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgist is an expert in or leader of public worship, its forms and rites.

clue.text: Ready in less than minute?

indicators.note: less than means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: minute, said my-NEWT, means very small, tiny

explanation.surface: Something might be ready in under a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like sixty seconds but is the adjective meaning tiny. 'Ready' is British slang for cash, as is TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old British slang terms for money: ready money and tin.

clue.text: Very good to avoid moronic boss

indicators.note: the stupid word steers clear of the very-good letters, which are removed

parts.note: moronic means stupid
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: It's very good to stay away from a dim-witted manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is not a manager but a raised ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud and a boss are both a projecting knob or rounded ornament on a surface.

clue.text: Sailor chasing duck, suggesting absence of duties

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the sailor follows the duck

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman runs after a duck, hinting that no work is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero-rating is a tax status meaning goods carry no VAT, so no duty is levied.

clue.text: Nice line taken by one beginning on astronomy in Oxford college

indicators.note: the line letter is taken up by, followed by, the numeral one

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the first letter of astronomy goes inside the college name

parts.note: Keble is a college of Oxford University

indicators.note: beginning on picks out the opening letter of astronomy

explanation.surface: A pleasant line taken by an astronomy beginner at an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and likeable are both synonyms for pleasant, agreeable.

clue.text: Curtailed complex argument in school

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, the last letter

parts.note: complex means hard, difficult
a row is an argument

explanation.surface: A shortened, complicated dispute takes place at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public (private, fee-paying) school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow School is one of England's best-known boarding schools, so it is an example of a school.

clue.text: Harry Potter most about one person displaying spectacles?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the numeral
to harry is to harass, so these words are worried into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Harry Potter, most of all, looks like a person wearing glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the wizard's name but is the anagram signal. 'about' puts the scrambled POTTERMOST around I.
explanation.definitionFit: An optometrist tests eyesight and sells glasses, so their shop displays spectacles.

clue.text: High, high point? It gives a buzz in recreation

definitions.text: It gives a buzz in recreation

parts.note: high, of meat or smells, means smelly; humming is British slang for smelly
the top is the highest point

explanation.surface: Someone high on something enjoys a peak experience giving them a buzz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like intoxicated; it means smelly, and HUMMING is British slang for that.
explanation.definitionFit: A humming top is a spinning toy that drones as it spins, a buzzing plaything.

clue.text: Exploits fish to make dairy drink

parts.note: to milk someone is to exploit them
hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of fish to make a drink from dairy products.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkshake is a cold blended drink made from milk, often with ice cream.

clue.text: People like you to look adult, not callow again, ultimately

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: not means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: People of your own age want to look grown-up, not naive again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives W and N, the last letters of 'callow' and 'again', which 'not' removes from GROWNUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer group is the set of people of your own age and status, those like you.

clue.text: Keen on India article being dumped by international body

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the article is thrown out of the alliance's name

parts.note: NATO is the international military alliance
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: India, keen on the idea, finds an article thrown out by an international organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is an informal way of being enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: A duck eating a catch

indicators.note: the word for nothing takes the letter A into itself

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nil

explanation.surface: A duck eats something it has caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a criminal is to catch them, an informal sense of the verb.

clue.text: One adding sentence in Gershwin number

parts.note: one who adds up is a summer, one who does sums
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A clerk totting up figures adds a phrase to a Gershwin song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' here is pronounced SUM-er, one who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Summertime is a famous aria from Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess.

clue.text: Following marriage, one moved elsewhere — being inclined to fight?

indicators.note: the numeral is taken out of its place and set down at another spot in the word

parts.note: marital describes the state that follows a wedding
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: After a wedding, one partner moved out, apparently spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved elsewhere' shifts the I of MARITAL two places along.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means warlike, relating to fighting, as in martial arts.

clue.text: Unreliable character's beginning on witness stand

indicators.note: beginning on picks the opening letter of witness

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A dodgy character is about to take the witness stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witness stand' reads as one courtroom phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person, from the animal's crafty reputation.

clue.text: Powerless mass accepting military leader's stand-in

indicators.note: the shortened mass takes the officer letters inside it
powerless means without P, the physics symbol for power

parts.note: a lump is a mass
OC is Officer Commanding, a military leader; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A weak mass of people accepts a substitute for their military chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who temporarily covers for another, a substitute.

clue.text: Control, say, brought into sport recently

indicators.note: the for-example letters are placed inside the rugby letters

parts.note: RU is rugby union
say means for example, eg
late means recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: Control was, so to speak, introduced into the game only recently.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate something is to control it by rules.

clue.text: Labouring under really grim illness at the outset — this one?

definitions.text: Labouring under really grim illness at the outset — this one?

indicators.note: at the outset picks the opening letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: Someone suffering a nasty illness wonders whether it is this particular one.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy, also spelt lurgi, is a jokey British name for an unspecified contagious ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: The dreaded lurgi is a humorous name for any vague infectious illness, a really grim one.

clue.text: China's upset after Russia's leader tucked into their Chairman's liqueur

indicators.note: the combined letters go inside the chairman's name

parts.note: Chairman Mao led the Chinese, so he is their chairman; the 's reads as 'is'

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come after the Russian initial
leader picks the first letter of the word Russia
upset means the letters of the word are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: An upset China follows Russia's leader into their chairman's drinks cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their Chairman' borrows China from earlier in the clue: Mao was Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a clear cherry liqueur from Dalmatia.

clue.text: Diplomatic behaviour, heading off legislation

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: tact is diplomatic, sensitive behaviour

explanation.surface: Diplomats behave by forestalling a new law.
explanation.definitionFit: An act is a law passed by Parliament, a piece of legislation.

clue.text: Listening, means to check for bad weather

indicators.note: listening tells us the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a rein is used to check, restrain, a horse

explanation.surface: Someone tuning in to the forecast checks whether bad weather is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is a common form of unwelcome, inclement weather.

clue.text: Insurance details, perhaps for specific little picture?

parts.note: the definite article picks out a specific thing
little means small
a print is a picture, an engraving or photograph

explanation.surface: Insurance terms are likened to a particular tiny picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specific' stands for the definite article, which singles out one particular thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine print of a policy holds its detailed conditions and exclusions, which insurers are accused of hiding.
